chapter: Studio recordings of the late twenties and thirties
title: Victor Young and recording for ARC, Brunswick and Decca
summary: He knew Victor Young well as a good leader of a recording orchestra, and recorded across ARC, Brunswick and Decca from acoustic days on.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: No, okay. Victor Young and his orchestra, do you remember Victor Young?
Victor Young, I know him well.
You know him well. Tell me about Victor Young. What kind of person, what kind of musician?
He's a very good musician.
How about working for him?
Working for him, he's a very good orchestra leader.
Okay. And he was a composer as well.
Yeah. He went through all of this pink stuff.*
Yeah, I know what you mean.
You know, all of those things.
You did a lot of recording sessions. You didn't have an orchestra. It was a recording orchestra. Am I right?
Yeah.
And you didn't play dance dates with them.
No.
Just recording.
Unless he would suggest a dance date.
Oh. Then you did some of those too.
Okay. Then you recorded for the ARC Brunswick and for Decca. Interesting, in doing this research on you Chauncey, I
* Refers to Mr. Kline's notes written in red ink.
Yes.
Which is pretty phenomenal. It shows you how you stretched from the acoustic recording into playing.
Sure.
